content: Women's suffrage was adopted at the federal level in Switzerland in **1971**. Swiss men voted in favor of granting women the right to vote in federal elections on February 7, 1971. However, women did not gain the right to vote in local cantonal matters until even later in some cantons, with the last canton (Appenzell Innerrhoden) finally granting women voting rights in local elections in 1991 following a decision by the Swiss Federal Supreme Court.
